2025.clinched: 8 Hours of Bahrain, 8 November 2025, final round (8 of 8)
2025.note: Calado, Giovinazzi and Pier Guidi had led the championship since winning at Imola in April, and fourth place in the Bahrain finale on 8 November 2025 settled it. The #51 Ferrari finished 26.5 seconds behind the winning #7 Toyota of Mike Conway, Kamui Kobayashi and Nyck de Vries. Ferrari's three crews locked out the top three places in the drivers' standings, and the marque took the manufacturers' title by 75 points: its first top-class world endurance championship since 1972. It was a fourth championship each for Pier Guidi and Calado, after their GT titles.

2024.clinched: 8 Hours of Bahrain, 2 November 2024, final round (8 of 8)
2024.note: Estre, Lotterer and Vanthoor finished eleventh in Bahrain on 2 November 2024, the #6 Porsche's worst result of the season, and were champions anyway, because their nearest rivals did not score either: the margin held at 35 points on a total of 150. Vanthoor had dropped to fourteenth after first-lap contact, Estre spent the middle of the race recovering the places, and two late safety cars plus two penalties undid the work. They had led the standings from the opening round in Qatar. Toyota took the manufacturers' title, 190 to Porsche's 184, and it was Lotterer's last race as a Porsche works driver.

2023.clinched: 8 Hours of Bahrain, 4 November 2023, final round (7 of 7)
2023.note: Buemi, Hartley and Hirakawa won the Bahrain finale on 4 November 2023 from pole, leading every lap outside the pit cycles, which is the most direct way a championship can be settled. It was effectively over at the start: Earl Bamber's Cadillac locked up into Turn 1 and spun the sister #7 Toyota as it tried to hold second. The #7 recovered to second for a Toyota one-two, 47 seconds back, having won four races that season to the #8's two — a retirement at double-points Le Mans is what cost them. Fourth titles for Buemi and Hartley, a second for Hirakawa.

2022.clinched: 8 Hours of Bahrain, 12 November 2022, final round (6 of 6)
2022.note: Buemi, Hartley and Hirakawa arrived at the Bahrain finale tied on 121 points with the Alpine of André Negrão, Matthieu Vaxivière and Nicolas Lapierre, which turned out to be the slowest Hypercar in the field and could only finish third. So they did not need to win, and were told not to: Toyota asked the #8 to let the faster #7 through in the third hour, and they came home second, 45 seconds adrift, on 12 November 2022. It was the hundredth race in the championship's history. Third titles for Buemi and Hartley; Hirakawa took his in his first season in the category.

2021.clinched: 8 Hours of Bahrain, 6 November 2021, final round (6 of 6)
2021.note: Conway, Kobayashi and López needed only to be classified. Pole on the Friday had taken their lead over the sister #8 Toyota to sixteen points, so second place behind it in the Bahrain finale on 6 November 2021, 7.351 seconds back, was more than enough. Conway led the early running and was asked to hand the place to a faster Buemi at the start of the second hour. They were the first Hypercar champions, in the class's first year, and it was back to back for the trio after 2020. The race was Kazuki Nakajima's last for Toyota.

2020.clinched: 8 Hours of Bahrain, 14 November 2020, final round (8 of 8)
2020.note: Conway, Kobayashi and López went to the last race six points behind the sister #8 Toyota, whose championship lead had earned it a success handicap worth about half a second a lap. They took pole, led from lights to flag and won by 1m 04s, which turned the deficit into a five-point championship on 107 points. It was the final race of the LMP1 era before Hypercar replaced it. López became the third person to win drivers' titles in two different FIA world championships, and Conway the first British champion in the class since Anthony Davidson in 2014.

2019.clinched: 24 Hours of Le Mans, 16 June 2019, final round of the 2018-19 super season (8 of 8)
2019.note: The only time Le Mans has served as the championship finale. Buemi, Alonso and Nakajima needed seventh place and won the race instead, by 17 seconds, after the leading sister #7 Toyota lost time to a puncture its own sensors had reported on the wrong corner: the crew changed the front-right, the damage was at the left-rear, and it had to stop again the following lap. They had led the standings since the super season opened in May 2018, and finished on 198 points to the #7 crew's 157. It was Alonso's first championship in thirteen years, and his last race for Toyota.

2017.clinched: 6 Hours of Shanghai, 5 November 2017, one round to spare (round 8 of 9)
2017.note: Bernhard, Bamber and Hartley were running third at Shanghai on 5 November 2017, which was already enough, when José María López's Toyota took left-rear suspension damage and pitted, promoting the #2 Porsche to second. That left a 32-point lead with only 26 still available at the Bahrain finale. The #8 Toyota won the race by over a lap. Porsche took a third consecutive manufacturers' title the same afternoon. It was a second championship for Bernhard and Hartley, who had won in 2015 alongside Mark Webber, and Hartley added Le Mans to it that year.

2016.clinched: 6 Hours of Bahrain, 19 November 2016, final round (9 of 9)
2016.note: Lieb, Dumas and Jani took the title in sixth place, after contact with the KCMG Porsche in the second hour of the Bahrain finale on 19 November 2016. A 17-point lead meant fifth would have been enough even if Toyota had won and taken the pole point. Their season was really two races: they won at Silverstone and then Le Mans, left Le Mans with 94 points from a possible 103, and never reached a podium again. The race itself was Audi's last in endurance racing and Audi won it, while Mark Webber finished third in the last race of his professional career.

2015.clinched: 6 Hours of Bahrain, 21 November 2015, final round (8 of 8)
2015.note: Bernhard, Webber and Hartley had won four in a row at the Nürburgring, Austin, Fuji and Shanghai, and pole in Bahrain on 21 November 2015 stretched their lead to thirteen points. Then Bernhard lost nine laps in the opening hour to a throttle actuator problem, and Webber had to bring the car back into the garage in the closing two hours before nursing it home fifth. It held, by five points. The sister Porsche of Lieb, Dumas and Jani won the race. It was Porsche's first world championship since 1986.

2014.clinched: 6 Hours of Bahrain, 15 November 2014, one race to spare (round 7 of 8)
2014.note: Davidson and Buemi spent sixteen laps of the Bahrain race in the garage having an alternator changed, lost more than half an hour, finished eleventh, and were champions. Their only remaining rivals, the Audi crew of André Lotterer, Benoît Tréluyer and Marcel Fässler, had to finish second or better and came fourth. The sister Toyota of Alexander Wurz, Stéphane Sarrazin and Mike Conway won the race on 15 November 2014, Toyota's fifth win of the season. Davidson had never won a championship in car racing before. Toyota settled the manufacturers' title at the São Paulo finale two weeks later.

2013.clinched: 6 Hours of Shanghai, 9 November 2013, one race to spare (round 7 of 8)
2013.note: McNish, Kristensen and Duval needed third place at Shanghai on 9 November 2013 and finished exactly there, behind their own team-mates André Lotterer, Marcel Fässler and Benoît Tréluyer, who won the race. Audi had already settled the manufacturers' title in Japan three weeks earlier. The trio's season was built on winning Le Mans from pole, Kristensen's record ninth victory in the race. At the Bahrain finale their car stopped out on the circuit, so they never took a chequered flag as world champions.

2012.clinched: 6 Hours of Shanghai, 28 October 2012, final round (8 of 8)
2012.note: The first World Endurance Championship went to Lotterer, Tréluyer and Fässler in the last race of 2012, where third place at Shanghai on 28 October held off their Audi team-mates Allan McNish and Tom Kristensen. Alexander Wurz and Nicolas Lapierre won the race for Toyota, having pushed Audi hard through the second half of the season. Audi had been out of reach in the manufacturers' championship since August, with five wins and five poles from the eight rounds, and its eleventh Le Mans victory that June was the first there by a hybrid car.
